newsitem.title: FRANCE: Moslem rebels in Algeria kill eight including baby.
newsitem.headline: Moslem rebels in Algeria kill eight including baby.

text.p: Suspected Moslem fundamentalists killed eight people, including a 13-month-old baby, in a night attack outside Algiers, Algerian security forces said on Friday.
In a statement, security officials said the eight were "assassinated in a cowardly way" -- the term Algeria normally uses for killings in which the victims have their throats cut.
"This barbarous act did not exclude a baby of 13 months who was strangled by the criminals," said the statement, carried on the official Algerian news agency APS.
The attack took place in the farming community of Sidi Kaddour in Sidi Moussa district, in Blida province, during the night of Wednesday-Thursday.

The provincial capital Blida, some 50 km (30 miles) south of Algiers, is the headquarters of the Algiers military district and a known stronghold of Moslem fundamentalists who have been trying for five years to topple the Algerian authorities.
A retired Algerian general was killed on Thursday in the western city of Oran soon after a state funeral in Algiers for assassinated union leader Abdelhak Benhamouda.
Benhamouda, a vociferous anti-Islamist, had recently said that the political hierarchy had done nothing to resolve five years of crisis in which about 60,000 people have been killed.
The violence began in 1992 after the authorities cancelled a general election dominated by Islamists. New elections are promised before July this year.
